content: Puffing is a method used to draw smoke, typically from tobacco products, into the oral cavity. Through this process, nicotine is absorbed, and the flavors present in the tar particles can be detected. After a brief period, usually lasting only a few seconds, the smoke is expelled from the mouth. When smoking cigars or pipes, individuals typically take a draw every few minutes, depending on personal preference, though some may choose to do so less frequently. Unlike cigarette smoking, the smoke is generally not inhaled directly into the lungs. Instead, the focus during puffing is primarily on savoring the taste. For this reason, many types of tobacco are enhanced with added flavors and aromas, such as vanilla, to enrich the sensory experience.
